films.title: Blossom
films.description: Treatment Skateboards' 18-minute full-length follows the Glasgow collective through two years of filming, a changing team and the arrival of spring 2026. Eight Treatment riders anchor the film alongside eight documented friends, with sessions and trips spanning Glasgow, Fife, Edinburgh, Newcastle and Scotland's central belt.
creditNotes: The licensed Skateboarder's Companion premiere and its first-person Treatment feature supply the eight team riders, the friends roster, Dean Mackie's filming/editing credit and the two-year production history.

The exact film's end-title roll was visually reviewed to preserve Sean McDonald, Cammy Lambie and Kechnie beyond the abbreviated upload description and to document the supported additional camera credits.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies Blossom as a 2026 full-length and indexes all 16 skaters plus the production credits. It normalizes Scotch under Seaghan Crawley; this record preserves the first-party nickname and spelling. No unsupported formal director credit is asserted.
films.locationNote: Treatment and Dean Mackie's first-person feature documents regular filming in Glasgow, Fife, Edinburgh and Scotland's central belt, a four-day Newcastle trip and an Aberdeen caption; no unsupported spot-by-spot itinerary is asserted.
films.historicalContext: Filmed across 2024 and 2025 while Treatment's ownership and team evolved, Blossom marks the young Glasgow collective's next chapter and introduced newer riders Beth Walker and Oskar Waren within a wider Scottish and northern-English scene film.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1920x1080 YouTube max-resolution artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-16. It is Kerr Melville's credited cover photograph of Oskar Waren kickflipping at night and contains no trailer or episode labeling.

films.title: BACK THEN
films.description: Dan Schulz's 22-minute Berlin full-length brings together 24 skaters across generations and scenes, led by a part from German veteran Sami Harithi. Filmed and edited by Schulz, the independent video also features Tim Janke, Michi Mackrodt, Leo Romero, Wes Kremer, Valeri Rosomako and a broad Berlin-centered cast.
creditNotes: Dan Schulz's filmmaker-channel upload explicitly identifies BACK THEN as a full-length, credits Schulz with filming and editing and supplies all 24 named appearances.
Free Skate Magazine and Skate Jawn independently identify the work as Schulz's Berlin full-length and repeat the complete roster, with Free highlighting Sami Harithi's featured part.

The official description thanks Nils Werner, David Lichtenauer, Dominik Grube and Nicklas Stinner without assigning formal roles, so they are preserved in source notes rather than promoted to production credits.
films.locationNote: Both Free Skate Magazine and Skate Jawn explicitly identify the film as a Berlin video; no unsupported spot-by-spot itinerary is asserted.
